also: I have a confession to make

terms.comment: An admission of a fault or of anything else, with the genitive of what is admitted.

evidence: Mart. 4.49.10: cōnfiteor: laudant illa, sed ista legunt
terms.comment: The verb: to admit, own up; in the Church also to confess sins and to praise God.

phrases.latin: nec vultūs modo ac vōcis exprimit cōnfessiōnem, sed tōtum corpus vī suā concutit
phrases.english: laughter forces a confession not only from the face and voice, but shakes the whole body

phrases.latin: Sī rem ipsam ingenuē cōnfiteāre, forsitan dēlictī grātiam faciet.
phrases.english: If you just own up frankly, perhaps he’ll let you off.

sources: Lewis & Short: confessio · Lewis & Short: confiteor
